provenance.locator: Recommendation 4 (solitary part-solid lung nodules): "For nodules with particularly suspicious morphology (ie, lobulated margins or cystic components), a growing solid component, or a solid component larger than 8 mm, PET/CT, biopsy, or resection are recommended (grade 1B)." This rule governs only the solid-component->8mm alternative of this sentence; suspicious morphology and growing solid component are explicitly out of scope (no Clinical Input State field exists for either). No independent whole-nodule diameter threshold is stated by this sentence or elsewhere in Recommendation 4 for this state. Not present in the Local SOP text (see Governance Note).

provenance.locator: Recommendation 4, State A (whole nodule <6mm): "In practice, discrete solid components cannot be reliably defined in such small nodules, and they should be treated similar to the way in which pure ground-glass lesions of equivalent size are treated." Source basis for treating a missing solid-component measurement as not applicable, rather than a data gap, once whole-nodule diameter independently resolves below 6mm under fleischner-2017-average-diameter.

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner recommends, for a solitary, part-solid, incidental pulmonary nodule with a solid component greater than 8mm in diameter, in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised: further characterization by PET/CT, or biopsy/tissue sampling, or resection -- presented as coequal options with no source-stated ranking or timing between them. Recommendation 4 states no independent whole-nodule diameter threshold for this trigger; the whole-nodule diameter is not evaluated by this rule. This content is materially absent from the Local SOP text, which contains no escalation/PET-CT/biopsy content for part-solid nodules at all -- this rule's entire clinical basis is the primary Fleischner guideline.
